target_customer: Women who want non-invasive health testing, plus researchers and clinics running studies; sold direct and via FSA/HSA eligibility
problem: Blood tests require venipuncture or finger pricks, and menstrual blood, collected regularly, was unused as a diagnostic sample.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer diagnostic service: Q-Pad kit, lab analysis and results through an app, plus research partnerships

founders.name: Sara Naseri
founders.background_notes: Described as a physician in the product coverage; she is named on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a new sample type, collection device and clinical validation of biomarkers in menstrual blood, then FDA clearance.

defensibility.rationale: FDA 510(k) clearance, CE and UKCA marking and a biobank of samples are slow to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent pursued menstrual blood diagnostics; coverage says it is the first FDA-cleared menstrual blood testing device.

market_need_then: Company materials say there was virtually no published research on the diagnostic use of menstrual blood when the founder started, so the need was an untested hypothesis rather than a measured demand.

identity.visual_style: Medical consumer product, Q-Pad looks like an ordinary pad

branding.brand_signature: The Q-Pad, a menstrual pad that doubles as a test kit
branding.community_and_virality: TIME Best Inventions 2024 special mention (30 Oct 2024); coverage in Femtech Insider, BioSpace and Positive News.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press for a novel product, a TIME mention and trademarks on Q-Pad and Q-Strip, but limited consumer reach evidence.

outcome_analysis: Qvin built the Q-Pad menstrual blood test and won Thailand approval in 2023 and its first FDA clearance for Q-Pad and the A1c test in January 2024, with CE and UKCA marking and research studies in the US, UK and Denmark. The legal entity is Qurasense, Inc. It is active and still early, so success rests on regulatory clearance, while funding history is not verifiable from public sources.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators conflict (Seedtable 19.3M, Bouncewatch 12.27M venture round Mar 2021, The Company Check 12.42M over 3 rounds with a Series A Oct 2020, CB Insights 120K under a different name, VCBacked convertible note Apr 2024); no press release found, so no round is recorded. Aggregators label Qvin as YC S18 while the YC directory in this dataset says Winter 2016; the YC page itself was not checked for the batch conflict. Competitor list left empty: no source dated near 2016 for rivals; Papcup is mentioned only in later coverage. Founder education and prior employers not found.
